MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, Housing
  Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  March 25, 2025
A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the Successor
Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the Library Board of
Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Ruesch at 5:00 p.m.,
on March 25, 2025, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted by 5:00
p.m. on March 20, 2025, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. A copy was also posted at the
Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive and Norman P. Murray Community
and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Goodell
  Council Member Kelley
  Council Member Vasquez (arrived at 5:10 pm)
  Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum
  Mayor Ruesch

Absent:  Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum (left the meeting at 7:05 pm)

Staff Present:  Elaine Lister, City Manager
  Jerry Hill, Assistant City Manager
  William P. Curley, City Attorney
  Ellis Chang, Director of Administrative Services
  Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk
  Renata Winter, Assistant City Clerk

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that following Consent Calendar item #14 for the Annual Routine
Tree Trimming Contract has some legal issues that the City has not had time to review and stated that it
will be removed from the agenda and will return at a future meeting.

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Labor Negotiations - The Council Will Provide Direction to its Labor Negotiator Pursuant to
  Government Code Section 54957 and 54957.6. The Parties to the Negotiations Are the City
  and City’s Unrepresented Employees. The City’s Negotiator is Elaine Lister.

City Council Minutes  1  March 25, 2025
 CS2. Conference with Legal Counsel - Existing Litigation Paragraph (1) of subdivision (d) of Section
  54956.9 Janice Kronik Gath, et. al v. Mission Viejo OCSC Case No. 30-2024-01376969-CU-
  MC-CJC

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the time of 5:01 Mayor Ruesch recessed to Closed Session. At the time of 6:02 Mayor Ruesch
reconvened the meeting with all five Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley reported that CS1 was regarding Labor Negotiations and the Council was
updated and given direction. CS2 was regarding conference with legal counsel and the Council was
updated and given direction.

INVOCATION: Council Member Goodell

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Ruesch

PRESENTATIONS

P1. Update on Sober Living Legislation

  Received presentation from President of Venture Strategic Jeff Corless.

Mayor Ruesch, with the consensus of the Council, announced that Item #17 will be heard and considered
at this time.

PUBLIC HEARING (taken out of order)

17. Group Home and Sober Living Home Regulations

  Director of Planning & Community Development Larry Longenecker presented the staff report.

  Mayor Ruesch opened the Public Hearing at 6:27 pm

  Tanya Wills, M.V.: Addressed the Council with her concerns over two sober living homes on her
  street and asked if there would be any punitive damage to the owners who don’t abide by the
  ordinance’s stipulations.

  Mayor Ruesch closed the Public Hearing at 6:33 pm

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to (1) find that
  the project is exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) pursuant to state
  CEQA guidelines Section 15061(b)(3); and (2) introduce Ordinance 25-354 Rescinding and
  Revoking the Existing Chapter 5.06 Of Title 5 of the Mission Viejo Municipal Code and Adopting

City Council Minutes  2  March 25, 2025
   a New Chapter 5.06 of Title 5 of the Mission Viejo Municipal Code Titled "Group Home And Sober
  Living Home Regulations" and Related Findings.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

Mayor Ruesch asked Fire Chief Cheyne Maule to give an update on the newly released State Fire Severity
Maps by CalFire. Mayor Reusch mentioned that there will be a Town Hall Meeting on May 19 to discuss
the maps and get feedback from residents.

Mayor Ruesch also announced that the staggering of voting districts for the next election will be addressed
after the summer hiatus at the end of August or September.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Carolyn Gatto, M.V.: Spoke out against the individual that stole her sign at a rally. She asked what the
Council will do to allow residents to exercise their first amendment rights. She asked that a law
enforcement officer attend these rallies every Wednesday.

June Anderson, M.V.: Thanked Council Member Goodell and staff member Corey Gonyea for their
immediate response in contacting her regarding the lack of landscape maintenance at the end of the Oso
Creek Golf Course.

Peggy O’Neill, M.V.: Spoke out against CUSD Trustee Judy Bullockus on her racial slur at a recent
Capistrano Unified School Board Meeting. She pointed out that this does not reflect positively on our City
and asked the City Council to ensure a full condemnation of Judy Bullockus.

Kristen Wilcox, M.V.: Questioned the Police Chief’s response from the last meeting regarding ICE raids.
Asked why the police blotter is not up to date and the justification of clock cameras and why there was no
public forum for this.

Melissa Fieber, M.V.: Spoke out against Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum’s comments at the last meeting
regarding immigrants and ICE raids. She called the City Council to lead by example and asked that her
concerns be followed up.

Michele Mitchell, M.V.: Spoke on agenda item 18, the renaming of the dive well at the Marguerite
Aquatics Center and outlined why they authored this request for Dr. Ronald Brian.

Michael Schlesinger, M.V.: Commented on Council Member Goodell’s comments from the last meeting
regarding district voting. He clarified that the court struck down the two-year extension and that Council
Member Goodell and Kelley ran for a four-year term like everyone else. He asked if Ms. Bucknum has
ever repaid the City while she sat illegally on Council from 2020-2022 and if she has not then why?

City Council Minutes  3  March 25, 2025
 Dan Weerasekera, M.V.: Introduced himself as one of the Directors for the Mission Viejo Girls Softball
League. He thanked the City Council for supporting the League along with staff members Barbara
Swanson, Brian Zahn, Corey Gonyea, and Aumee Frey.

Cathy Palmer, M.V.: Addressed her concerns as to waiting to establish the staggering of districts in the
Fall and suggested that this be done in May or June.

Stacy Holmes, M.V.: Spoke out on CUSD Board Member Judy Bullockus on her racial slur at a board
meeting. Asked that the Council Member’s speak out against this and voiced concerns over how our City
will be viewed.

Carlos Pianelli, M.V.: Asked that the City Council invite Congresswoman Young Kim for a town hall
meeting so that her constituents can ask questions regarding social security and other funding cuts
happening in the current administration.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Item #15 was removed for a separate discussion.

Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Goodell to approve the Consent
Calendar outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  Bucknum

1.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of March 11, 2025, as presented.

2.  General Check Register Dated February 28, 2025, in the Amount of $655,624.55

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

3.  General Check Register Dated March 7, 2025, in the Amount of $3,592,969.14

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  Golf Check Register Dated February 28, 2025, in the Amount of $7,683.69

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

5.  Golf Check Register Dated March 7, 2025, in the Amount of $326,679.61

  Ratified the accompanying check register.
City Council Minutes  4  March 25, 2025
 6.  General Plan Progress Report for 2024

  Received report and directed staff to submit it to the state Office of Planning and Research (OPR)
  and state Housing and Community Development (HCD) by April 1, 2025.

7.  Annual Road and Flood Control Maintenance Contract

  (1) Approved Third Amendment, County Agreement #MA-080-23010587, with the County of
  Orange for the period July 1, 2025 through June 30, 2027 in the amount of $2,155,254.00; and (2)
  authorized issuance of a purchase order to the County of Orange for the period of July 1, 2025
  through June 30, 2026 in an amount not to exceed $1,077,627.00, pending adoption of the 2025-
  2027 budget by City Council.

8.  Annual Routine Monthly Landscape Maintenance - Contract Areas 9 & 10

  (1) Approved Fourth Amendment to the existing maintenance contract with Nieves Landscape, Inc.
  for the period of July 1, 2025 through June 30, 2027 to increase the contract amount by an amount
  not to exceed $2,160,674.00; (2) authorized issuance of a purchase order for Landscape Contract
  Area 9 to Nieves Landscape, Inc. for the period of July 1, 2025 through June 30, 2026, in an amount
  not to exceed $547,667.00 pending adoption of the 2025-2027 budget by City Council; and (3)
  authorized issuance of a purchase order for Landscape Contract Area 10 to Nieves Landscape, Inc.
  for the period of July 1, 2025 through June 30, 2026, in an amount not to exceed $532,670.00 pending
  adoption of the 2025-2027 budget by City Council.

9.  Annual Routine Janitorial and Related Services at Various Park Sites and Facilities

  (1) Approved the Eleventh Amendment for the Annual Routine Janitorial and Related Services at
  Various Park Sites and Facilities contract to Vocational Visions for the period of July 1, 2025 to
  June 30, 2027 in an amount not to exceed $417,522.00; and (2) authorized staff to issue a purchase
  order to Vocational Visions for the period of July 1, 2025 through June 30, 2026 in an amount not
  to exceed $203,669.00, pending adoption of the 2025-2027 budget by the City Council.

10. Annual Routine Playground, Parkland, and Facility Infrastructure Maintenance and Repairs

  (1) Approved Sixth Amendment to the existing contract with Jamey Clark, Inc., for the period of
  July 1, 2025 through June 30, 2027 in the amount of $919,849.00; and (2) authorized issuance of a
  purchase order to Jamey Clark, Inc., for the period of July 1, 2025 through June 30, 2026, in an
  amount not to exceed $459,924.00, pending adoption of the 2025-2027 budget by City Council.

11. Annual Routine Park, Right-of-Way, and Electrical Facility, Lighting Maintenance Repair
  and Replacement

  (1) Approved Fourth Amendment to the existing contract for the subject services to Real Estate
  Consulting and Services, Inc. for the period of July 1, 2025 through June 30, 2027 in the amount of
  $643,110.00; and (2) authorized issuance of a purchase order to Real Estate Consulting and Services,

City Council Minutes  5  March 25, 2025
   Inc. for the period of July 1, 2025 through June 30, 2026 in an amount not to exceed $321,555.00
  pending adoption of the 2025-2027 budget by City Council.

12. Annual Routine Fleet Vehicle Maintenance Services

  (1) Approved Third Amendment to the existing contract for the subject services to Mission Viejo
  Service Centers, Inc. for the period of July 1, 2025 through June 30, 2027 in the amount of
  $163,200.00; and (2) authorized issuance of a purchase order to Mission Viejo Service Centers, Inc.
  for the period of July 1, 2025 through June 30, 2026 in an amount not to exceed $81,600.00 pending
  adoption of the 2025-2027 budget by City Council.

13. Annual Routine Janitorial and Related Services at City Facilities

  (1) Approved Thirteenth Amendment to the existing maintenance contract with Alliance Building
  Maintenance, LLC for the subject services for the period of July 1, 2025 through June 30, 2027 in
  the amount of $1,534,294.77 and (2) authorized issuance of a purchase order to Alliance Building
  Maintenance, LLC for the period of July 1, 2025 through June 30, 2026, in an amount not to exceed
  $767,147.38 pending adoption of the 2025-2027 budget by City Council.

16. Traffic Signal Synchronization Project Expenditure Extension

  Authorized the Director of Public Works to submit a request to the Orange County Transportation
  Authority to extend the expenditure deadlines for Measure M2 Fiscal Year 2025-2026 for the
  Ongoing Maintenance and Monitoring Phase of the Marguerite Parkway & Olympiad Road-Felipe
  Road Traffic Signal Synchronization Projects.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

15. Purchase and Installation of Air Conditioning Equipment for the Oso Creek Golf Course
  Atrium Building

  Director of Public Services Jerry Hill presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Goodell, seconded by Council Member Vasquez, to (1) award the
  contract to Tri-Pacific Heating & Air Conditioning, L.P., for the Installation of Carrier Air
  Conditioning Equipment and Controls for the Oso Creek Golf Course Atrium building in an amount
  not to exceed $69,426.00; and (2) approve the First Amendment to David Electric in an amount not
  to exceed $40,000.00 to provide electrical installation services for the Atrium building Air
  Conditioning Equipment.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Bucknum

NEW BUSINESS
City Council Minutes  6  March 25, 2025
 18. Request to Name the Marguerite Aquatics Complex Dive Well after Dr. Ron O’Brien

  Director of Recreation and Community Services Mark Nix presented the staff report.

  Council Member Goodell recused himself from this item due to a conflict of interest and left the dais
  at 7:40 pm

  Council Member Vasquez asked questions as to the policy on the naming of city facilities and
  questioned if the financial summary that she had asked for when the most recent Nadadores
  agreement was approved has been received by the City.

  Nadadores’ Executive Director Michele Mitchell confirmed that reports have been sent and received
  at the expected time to the city per the agreement. Michele confirmed that Dr. Ron O’Brien did meet
  the requirements per the policy.

  Mayor Ruesch called for the vote and Council Member Vasquez asked for an amended motion to
  not cover the cost of the installation. This motion died for a lack of a second.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Ruesch, to Approve the naming of
  the Marguerite Aquatics Complex Dive Well after the late Dr. Ron O'Brien as recommended by the
  Community Services Commission, and (2) approve the applicant's request for the City to cover the
  installation costs of approximately $2,540 after they have paid for the signage.

  On roll call, said motion failed by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley and Ruesch
  NOES:  Vasquez
  ABSENT: Bucknum and Goodell

  Council Member Goodell returned to the dais at 7:49 pm

19.  Mid-Year Budget Review for FY 2024-2025

  Director of Administrative Services Ellis Chang presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Goodell, to adopt
  Resolution 25-06 Amending the FY 2024-25 Budget for Adjustments to Certain Revenue Sources
  and Operating and Capital Improvement Program Appropriations.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Bucknum

City Council Minutes  7  March 25, 2025
 MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

20. Orange County Local Agency Formation Commission (LAFCO) Report

  Received written report.

21. Southern California Association of Governments (SCAG) Report

  Received written report.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

22. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended ~ AB1234

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as
  presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public record.

Council Member Goodell

Nothing to report.

Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley attended the ribbon cutting for City Side Fiber which is a new fiber company in
the City. She attended the Night Market’s Saint Paddy’s Day on March 15 which was lots of fun. Council
Member Kelley commented that the night markets are very successful with great attendance along with
the farmers market on Saturday mornings. She attended the celebration of a new community Torah at the
Chabad in Mission Viejo which was very interesting and moving experience to see the Torah, which is
the first five books of the Bible written in Hebrew by a Scribe. She indicated that he had just finished it
while she attended the celebration and then they paraded through the street adjacent to the Jewish Center.
She said it was a wonderful event to support on behalf of the City.

Council Member Vasquez

Council Member Vasquez attended the Orange County Islamic Foundation dinner and really enjoyed the
event as she does every year. She was invited to an event at State Senator Blakespear’s office where she
was recognized as a woman who inspires. She indicated that someone within the community nominated
herself and she mentioned that Council Member Bucknum was also nominated.

Mayor Ruesch

Mayor Ruesch stated he was proud to represent the City at the Saddleback Scouting District Dinner on
March 13 which the City was awarded a certificate of appreciation for our support of scouting. He was
also given an award for 25 years of service with scouting. Last week he was up in Sacramento representing
the City in eleven different meetings on how we can get better support for Mission Viejo. He said it was
a very quick trip. Lastly, he concluded his comments with a quote from Mahatma Ghandi, “Be the change
that you wish to see in the world”.
City Council Minutes  8  March 25, 2025
 ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 8:02 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session, Mayor
Ruesch adjourned the meeting in Memory of Taffy Wilberg to Tuesday, April 8, 2025, at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________
Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of April 8, 2025

City Council Minutes  9  March 25, 2025
